narrative.weekly_mirror: This week held both practical care and moments where fairness seemed harder to carry through. You stayed back to help the peon uncle fix a broken desk, while later you “kept quiet because Sharma sir is senior” and, tired and wanting to finish quickly, spent “probably twice as much at a chain store” instead of waiting another day.
narrative.tension_explanation: The tension appears in how tiredness, hierarchy, and convenience shaped your choices: “I didn't have the energy to start something,” and “I just wanted to get it done fast.” These moments sit alongside your wish to make the world a fairer, better place, including the earlier realization after speaking with Didi that “we didn't talk about...” what might have mattered to her.
narrative.reflective_question: When tiredness, hierarchy, or convenience are present, what kinds of fairness become easiest for you to notice—and which become harder to act on?
